clue.text: Shop, strangely quiet after endless spree

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the shortened spree
without its end, so the final letter of the synonym for spree is dropped

parts.note: a drinking bout is a spree of indulgence

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of its normal order, so the letters of quiet are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper notices a store has gone oddly silent after a never-ending shopping spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of BOUT, and 'strangely' rearranges QUIET into TIQUE; the spree is a drinking-style bout, not a shopping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fashionable clothes shop is called by this French borrowing.

clue.text: Curious boy, very likely to succeed

parts.note: odd means curious or strange
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A strange lad who is expected to do well.
explanation.definitionFit: A betting term for a favourite whose odds are shorter than evens, so very likely to win.

clue.text: Food that may provide energy after excursion

indicators.note: puts the energy symbol after the excursion

parts.note: a trip is an excursion
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something to eat that may give you energy after an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow's stomach lining, eaten in Britain, is a traditional food.

clue.text: Eccentric open to suspicion before search

indicators.note: puts the suspicious word ahead of the search word

parts.note: queer once meant suspicious or questionable
to fish for something is to search for it

explanation.surface: An oddball comes under suspicion before a search.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd or peculiar person is an old idiom for an eccentric.

clue.text: English singer inside my diplomatic residence

indicators.note: the singer goes inside the word my

parts.note: a bass is a low-voiced singer

explanation.surface: An English singer is staying inside an ambassador's home.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official home and offices abroad is this building.

clue.text: Salad ingredient in a bowl right at the front

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for right goes first, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: a bowl is a dish

explanation.surface: A salad item sits in a bowl, with one placed right at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp red root vegetable is commonly sliced into salads.

clue.text: Queen standing up — better go over

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means the letters read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
to cap something is to better or outdo it

explanation.surface: Someone tells the Queen to stand, as it is better to go over things.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise again is to go over the main points briefly.

clue.text: Blue act entertaining crowd

indicators.note: the act word holds, as a host entertains, the crowd word

parts.note: a deed is an act
a press is a crowd or throng

explanation.surface: A sad performance being put on for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means feeling low or downcast in mood.

clue.text: Friendly Society, one having what it takes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
able means having what it takes, competent

explanation.surface: The Friendly Society, a member of which is capable.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly society is a British mutual savings and insurance association; 'Friendly Society' reads as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sociable enjoys company and is friendly.

clue.text: Wicked trait shown by a daughter's counsel

indicators.note: places the vice beside the a and daughter pieces

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees
a vice is a wicked trait of character

explanation.surface: A daughter's guidance reveals a wicked streak in her.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is guidance offered to someone, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Second team's kit carrier

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a pack is a team, as the forwards in rugby

explanation.surface: The reserve side's equipment bag, belonging to the second team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second team' reads as a reserve side, but 'Second' is the verb to support.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the back holds a hiker's gear or kit.

clue.text: A delicacy for ages, I suspect

indicators.note: what is suspect is not to be trusted as it stands, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone guesses a particular delicacy has been around for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Fattened goose or duck liver is a famous French luxury food.

clue.text: Page on wonderful bungalow, perhaps

parts.note: re means on or concerning
fab is informal for wonderful

explanation.surface: A page praising a bungalow as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefabricated house, often single-storey, is an example of a bungalow, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Method of carrying out home improvements? Study loo fire damaged

definitions.text: Method of carrying out home improvements?

indicators.note: damaged things are broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fire has damaged the study and toilet, so home repairs are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: DIY is doing home repairs and improvements oneself rather than hiring tradesmen.

clue.text: Democrat is vulgar, reportedly, in speech

indicators.note: signals the word for vulgar is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: coarse means vulgar or crude

explanation.surface: A Democrat's speech is said to be crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' swaps COARSE for its sound-alike COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is formal talk or a lecture, a synonym for speech.

clue.text: Fluctuating throughout

definitions.meaning: all over, as in travelling the length of the land

explanation.definitionFit: Both a varying state and all over an area, as in 'the length of the country'.

clue.text: Little person having to hitchhike, covering miles

indicators.note: the pieces go round, covering, the miles letter

parts.note: to thumb a lift is to hitchhike

explanation.surface: A short person must hitchhike, covering many miles.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM THUMB is the thumb-sized hero of an English folk tale, used for any tiny person.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk-tale character's name is used for a very small person.

clue.text: Put up other half, maybe, for one who's not the breadwinner?

parts.note: to house someone is to put them up
a husband is one example of a spouse or other half

explanation.surface: Giving a partner a home, as he is not the one earning the money.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who stays home to look after the household while his partner earns is not the breadwinner.

clue.text: Cash — shilling — Scrooge's clerk hasn't got it

parts.note: S was the abbreviation for the old British shilling

indicators.note: the clerk's name loses the following word

parts.note: Bob Cratchit is Scrooge's clerk in Dickens's A Christmas Carol

explanation.surface: Scrooge's clerk complains he has no money, not even a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't got' takes IT from CRATCHIT. A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch is informal slang for money, as in 'earning some scratch'.

clue.text: All so relaxed before start of major ski race

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go ahead of that opening letter
relaxed means loosened out of its rigid form, so these letters are rearranged
takes only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Everyone is so laid-back before a big ski race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill race weaving between gates is a type of ski race.

clue.text: Mighty clear

explanation.definitionFit: Both mighty in power and clear or compelling, as in a strong argument.

clue.text: Leg of mutton American soldier acquired

parts.note: GI is a US soldier
got means acquired

explanation.surface: A US soldier picks up a joint of lamb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigot is a French culinary term for a leg of lamb or mutton.

clue.text: Mock regulation restricting DI back in charge

indicators.note: the regulation word encloses and so restricts the other pieces

parts.note: a rule is a regulation

indicators.note: the letters DI are read backwards

explanation.surface: A rule keeps a detective inspector back from taking charge, which is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: The detective inspector looks like a person in the story, but is just two letters that 'back' turns round before they go into the regulation word.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to make fun of them, the verb sense.

clue.text: She's desperately after clubs in game

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the clubs letter

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: acting desperately means flailing about, so the letters of the clue word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman playing a game is desperate to follow clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players.

clue.text: Total published correctly

parts.note: a book that is out has been published
done right is done correctly

explanation.surface: A total figure has been published, and correctly so.
explanation.definitionFit: An outright win is a total, complete one, as adjectives.

clue.text: Too old? Absolutely, about 50

indicators.note: the word for absolutely goes round the numeral

parts.note: very means absolutely, as in the very best
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether turning fifty makes one too old, and the reply is absolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: Overly means excessively, the same sense as too in 'too keen'.

clue.text: Wretched sailor caught boarding fast plane

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: the caught letter gets on, inside, the plane

parts.note: a jet is a fast plane
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A miserable seaman is caught boarding a jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Abject describes a miserable, hopeless and wretched state.

clue.text: Good-looking cards dealt thus, by me

indicators.note: places the pieces next to each other

parts.note: a hand is the set of cards dealt to a player
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A card player reports how the cards were dealt to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome is attractive or good-looking in appearance.
